To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the invisible Higgs can be discovered in weak boson fusion at the 7 (8) TeV LHC if the branching fraction is above 40 % (60 %) and that the 7 and 8 TeV Lhc can probe branching fractions of 40 % and 60 % respectively, for the case where the Higgs decays invisibly with a branching fraction of 100 %.
the LHC has excellent potential to discover or exclude a SM-like Higgs decaying to invisible final states.

the 7 Tev LHC has a potential to observe an invisible SM-like Higgs boson with a branching fraction as small as 30% at a 5 sigma significance for a mass of about 120 GeV. The 8 Tev LHC can observe the same signal at a 5-sigma significance with a branching fraction down to 15%.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question: what can the LHC do in 2012 to measure the invisible Higgs decay width?
the discovery potential for the invisible Higgs decay mode in Higgs boson production at the 7, 8 TeV and 14 TeV LHC.
the search for a SM-like Higgs decaying to invisible particles.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 7 Tev LHC has a good potential to observe a Higgs boson with an invisible branching fraction of 40% or larger in the 120-170 GeV mass range.
the LHC is poised to discover a SM-like Higgs boson, or to exclude a Higgs boson in the 120-170 GeV mass range, with a 125 GeV SM-like Higgs decaying to invisible particles at the level of 20-40 %.

the 8 Tev LHC is not likely to observe a SM-like Higgs decaying invisibly, but it will be able to set a limit on the invisible Higgs rate at a level that would allow the 14 Tev LHC to discover the invisible Higgs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the LHC is sensitive enough to observe a SM-like Higgs boson with an invisible branching fraction of 20–40 % for a wide range of Higgs masses, but that the LHC will not be able to probe branching fractions much larger than 40 %.
the LHC will have a very good chance to discover an invisibly-decomposing Higgs in the near future.

the 8 Tev LHC has a similar sensitivity to an invisible Higgs boson as the 7 Tev LHC and the 8 Te V LHC has a better discovery potential for a Higgs with substantial branching fraction to invisible final state.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the LHC will be able to observe a SM-like Higgs with substantial invisible branching fractions at both 7 and 10 TeV.
the LHC has the potential to probe an invisibly-decomposing Higgs boson at the TeV scale.
the 7 Tev LHC has the potential to observe a light Higgs with an invisible branching fraction as high as 40 %.
